newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura says US SEC in routine inspection of unit.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says US SEC in routine inspection of unit.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd confirmed on Thursday that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) was making a routine inspection of its U.S. subsidiary.
A Nomura spokesman also said that the U.S. SEC has not told the company that it would annul the brokering and dealing licences held by Nomura Securities International Inc, Nomura's U.S. subsidiary.

Earlier on Thursday, Tetsundo Iwakuni, a member of Japan's opposition Sun Party, told a parliamentary committee that the U.S. SEC may have uncovered some problems that could lead to cancellation of the unit's brokerage licence.
Iwakuni made the remarks when Yoshihisa Tabuchi, former Nomura president, was summoned to speak before the budget committee as an unsworn witness regarding Nomura's racketeer payoff scandal.
The Nomura spokesman said that the SEC has been conducting routine inspections of several Nomura-related companies in the United States, including Nomura Securities International.
"These are routine inspections and they are not related to the current incident (the payoff scandal)," he said. He gave no further details.
Nomura is currently at the centre of a scandal involving suspected payoffs to corporate racketeers.
